chain.label: FAA oversight could not detect SOP noncompliance
chain.trigger: the POI "had never done an en route inspection of Trans-Pacific or any other Part 135 operator"; as of February 2019 the SAS had not been fully implemented for Part 135

chain.label: Operator had no SMS, FDM, or formal safety programs
chain.trigger: "no formal safety programs were in place at the time of the accident. Therefore, the company did not identify or mitigate the hazards that contributed to this accident"

chain.label: Both pilots' documented training deficiencies left unmonitored
chain.trigger: "both pilots began line operations without any further monitoring or evaluation" after requiring extra simulator sessions (PIC: circling approaches; SIC: aircraft control)

caused_by.evidence: "Trans-Pacific did not oversee the pilots' performance after their additional initial training to determine whether the noted performance deficiencies were fully resolved"
"the FAA's ineffective SAS procedures, which failed to identify these company oversight deficiencies"

chain.label: PIC allowed unapproved SIC-0 to act as pilot flying
chain.trigger: "okay I think we're next man. hand on your yoke"; "the PIC's decision to allow the SIC to act as PF was improper and contrary to company SOPs"

caused_by.evidence: "The company's lack of a method to discover noncompliance with the SIC policy may also have increased the opportunity for the flight crews' noncompliance."

chain.label: PIC's inadequate and incomplete preflight planning
chain.trigger: flight plan listed 28 minutes en route at 27,000 ft, "not compatible with each other"; no weather obtained before the PHL departure despite the 3-hour SOP requirement

caused_by.evidence: "Trans-Pacific would not have a way to identify this crew's deviations from policy and SOPs"

chain.label: Role reversal and constant coaching distracted the PIC from PM duties
chain.trigger: "the PIC's extensive coaching of the SIC in his PF duties distracted the PIC, interfered with the normal division of PF and PM duties, and degraded the flight crew's overall performance"

caused_by.evidence: "The PIC's decision to allow the SIC to act as PF placed both pilots in roles that they did not routinely perform."
"the SIC's performance of PF tasks was weak and required frequent coaching from the PIC"

chain.label: No approach briefing and required checklists omitted
chain.trigger: "the flight crew began the approach but did not conduct an approach briefing, which the operator's SOPs required for every approach and landing"; Climb, Cruise, and Descent checklists never called or performed

caused_by.evidence: "the PIC did not (1) effectively perform his PM role while he was coaching and directing the SIC because the PIC did not call for the Climb, Cruise, or Descent checklists"

chain.label: Navigation not set up and crew lost positional awareness of the approach
chain.trigger: "neither pilot detected that one of the navigation receivers was not tuned to the TEB VOR"; "the crew had not programmed the approach waypoints into the FMS flight plan before descent"; "I don't know what the # they thinkin' we're doin'"

caused_by.evidence: "This error might have been detected if an approach briefing had been conducted."
"This discussion indicates the pilots' lack of understanding of the route and positional awareness along the route (likely due to his poor preflight planning)."
"the time devoted to coaching the SIC during the short flight reduced time available for the PIC to ensure that he had an accurate understanding of the airplane's position and state"

chain.label: Vertical profile mismanaged; crossed fixes high and never captured glideslope
chain.trigger: "The airplane crossed DANDY at 2,050 ft and passed through the glideslope without capturing it"; crossed TORBY at 1,550 ft, "crossing an intermediate fix and the final approach fix hundreds of feet above the altitudes specified"

caused_by.evidence: "the pilots' failure to program the FMS might have also contributed to their poor positional awareness on the approach"

chain.label: Circle-to-land begun 2.8 nm past TORBY, airplane out of position
chain.trigger: "the airplane began the circle-to-land maneuver about 2.8 nm beyond TORBY (1 nm from the TEB runway 6 threshold)" contrary to the ATC instruction to circle at TORBY

caused_by.evidence: "the crew began the descent to the MDA from an altitude about 250 ft above the minimum crossing altitude for TORBY and continued to fly inbound toward the airport; thus, the MDA was reached when the airplane was beyond a position at which the crew could maneuver to runway 1 and fly a stabilized approach"
"the pilots seemed confused about the airplane's position on the approach, did not identify TORBY, and continued past the point at which they had been instructed to begin the circle-to-land maneuver"

chain.label: PIC continued the unstabilized approach instead of going around
chain.trigger: "the PIC's attempt to salvage an unstabilized visual approach"; neither pilot called for a go-around after the EGPWS "sink rate. pull up" alert

caused_by.evidence: "the PIC's decision to continue the approach was inappropriate because the approach did not meet the company's stabilized approach criteria and the airplane was not in a position to make a safe landing"

chain.label: Strong gusting northwesterly wind with no SOP wind additive
chain.trigger: tower reported "wind was from 360° at 16 kts gusting to 32 kts"; "the approach speeds listed in Trans-Pacific's SOPs did not include these wind additives"

chain.label: Steep low-altitude left turn with airspeed allowed to decay
chain.trigger: "the airplane reached a left bank angle of 35° and the airspeed decreased to about 111 kts"; "the PIC continued the left turn without adding power or lowering the airplane's nose to reduce AOA"

caused_by.evidence: "the rapid left turn was likely the PIC's attempt to continue the approach to landing"
"the left-wing-down aileron input required to make the turn to final and counter the strong (possibly gusting) left crosswind would have increased the right wing's AOA"

chain.label: Maneuvering at 350-450 ft agl with no recovery margin
chain.trigger: "the airplane reached a left bank angle of 35° at an altitude of 450 ft"; "resulting in an aerodynamic stall at low altitude"

chain.label: Aerodynamic stall during the turn to final
chain.trigger: "the PIC announced 'stall' in a strained voice"; "the PIC's focus on the visual maneuver of aligning the airplane with the landing runway distracted him from multiple indications of decreasing stall margin, resulting in an aerodynamic stall at low altitude"

caused_by.evidence: "Despite the SIC's airspeed callouts, the PIC continued the left turn without adding power or lowering the airplane's nose to reduce AOA."
"the strong, gusting wind might have momentarily reduced the airplane's airspeed below the stall speed"

chain.label: Departure from controlled flight, rolling right toward inverted
chain.trigger: "Witnesses reported seeing the airplane nearly inverted in a nose-low attitude just before impact"; the right wing stalling first "induc[ed] the airplane's roll to the right"

caused_by.evidence: "potentially led the wing to stall first, inducing the airplane's roll to the right (shown on radar data) just before impact"
stall occurred "at an altitude of 450 ft," leaving no altitude to recover

chain.label: Impact with commercial building and parking lot
chain.trigger: "impacted a commercial building and parking lot" about 0.5 mile south of runway 1; "The airplane was destroyed by impact forces and postcrash fire."

caused_by.evidence: "departed controlled flight while on a circling approach to runway 1 at Teterboro Airport... and impacted a commercial building and parking lot"

chain.label: Both pilots fatally injured
chain.trigger: "The pilot-in-command (PIC) and the second-in-command (SIC) died; no one on the ground was injured."

caused_by.evidence: "The cause of death for each pilot was multiple blunt trauma injuries."
